\begin{bankq}[id=SA07-P2-PHY-S1-Q04, source={Score Advanced - Test 07 (16 Apr 2023)}, paper=2, qno=4, type=multi, subtopic={Ohm's law}, answer={B,C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: atmospheric conduction with height-dependent conductivity, ohm's law, J times area is constant | steps: J times area is constant; Gauss's law for charge density}]
During fair weather conditions atmosphere of the Earth can be considered as a good conductor with resistivity $\rho$ depending on the height h from the surface of the Earth as $\dfrac{1}{\rho}$ = a + bh$^2$, where a and b are constants. It is also known that near the surface of the Earth is a downward electric field E$_0$, which causes a radial current in the atmosphere. Assume E$_0$ is constant in magnitude.\par
\bfig{73.0}{SA07_p2_phy_s1_q04_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The current density J decreases with increase in height.}
\opt{B}{The electrons will be travelling in radially outward direction.}
\opt{C}{The charge density will be negative at any general height.}

\begin{bankq}[id=TNAS02-P1-PHY-S1-Q03, source={TNAS - Test 02 (07 May 2023)}, paper=1, qno=3, type=single, subtopic={Ohm's law}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: relaxing charge density in a conductor | steps: Gauss law with decaying charge; displacement and conduction current; check each}]
Consider an isolated sphere of radius $b$, made of a material with permittivity $\varepsilon_0$ and electrical conductivity $\gamma$, whose volume charge density varies with time $t$ and is given as
\[\rho=\begin{cases}\rho_0e^{-t/\tau} & \text{if } 0\leqslant r<a\\ 0 & \text{if } a<r<\infty\end{cases}\]
Where $\tau=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0}{\gamma}$ and $0<a<b$. The spherical layer between radii $a$ and $b$ is neutral. Then choose the \textbf{incorrect} option.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The surface charge density at outer surface of sphere is $\dfrac{a^3\rho_0}{8b^2}$ at $t=\tau\,\ell n2$.}
\opt{B}{The total current in the region $0<r<a$ increases with the radius.}
\opt{C}{The electric field in the region $b<r<\infty$ is independent of time.}
\opt{D}{The total current in the region $a<r<b$ is independent of radius.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
